rounds.proof_sketch: feature_size=4096, THREADS=256, ELEMENTS_PER_THREAD=4. Loop processes 1024 elements per base iteration. base∈{0,1024,2048,3072}. Max element_idx = 3072 + 255*4 + 3 = 4095 < 4096. The boundary element_idx==4096 is never reached.
rounds.survival_reason: The mutation changes the boundary check from `<` to `<=`, which would allow processing when element_idx equals feature_size. However, with the fixed configuration (feature_size=4096, 256 threads, 4 elements per thread), the maximum element_idx computed is exactly 4095 (feature_size-1). Since 4096 divides evenly by 1024 (threads×elements_per_thread), all threads in the final iteration process exactly their full complement of valid elements without ever reaching the boundary case. The EMD Layer 2 divergence may be a false positive from floating-point non-determinism in the reduction operations.
rounds.kill_strategy: Unkillable with fixed shapes. The boundary case element_idx==feature_size requires feature_size to not be a multiple of THREADS*ELEMENTS_PER_THREAD (1024), but 4096%1024==0.
rounds.recommendations: When testing boundary condition mutations in GPU kernels, analyze whether the specific input dimensions make the boundary reachable. Mutation testing frameworks should include dimension-aware analysis to identify equivalent mutants caused by perfect alignment between data dimensions and kernel launch parameters.
